name: Sage
grown_as: Common sage, an evergreen shrubby herb. Drawn as the plain grey-green form. Purple sage ('Purpurascens'), gold ('Icterina') and three-coloured ('Tricolor') forms differ in leaf colour; broad-leaved forms rarely flower. ⚠️ CHECK
habit: A low, spreading, evergreen shrub 40 to 70 cm high and wider, woody at the base, the soft upper shoots square and downy.

leaf.type: Simple, sometimes with one or two small ear-like lobes at the base of the blade
leaf.outline: Oblong to narrowly oval, 3 to 8 cm long and 1 to 3 cm wide, sides almost parallel
leaf.margin: Very finely round-toothed all round, the teeth tiny
leaf.veins: A fine net of veins all pressed in, so the whole surface looks pebbled
leaf.surface: Thick, soft, finely felted; whiter and more woolly beneath

flower.form: A large two-lipped flower with a helmet-like upper lip
flower.petals: Joined; the upper lip straight or gently curved like a helmet; the lower lip three-lobed with a broad middle lobe
flower.centre: Stamens and style tucked under the helmet, the style tip just showing
flower.behind: A bell-shaped, two-lipped calyx, purple-tinged and sticky-hairy
flower.carried: In spaced rings of 4 to 8 up an upright spike 15 to 30 cm long at the shoot tips, held above the leaves

fruit: Round dark brown nutlets in the dry calyces.
winter: Evergreen: a low grey mound, some leaves browning.

leaf: an oblong leaf with a rounded tip on a clear stalk
pebbled surface from a net of pressed-in veins
tiny round teeth along the edge
bloom: a two-lipped violet-blue flower with a helmet-shaped upper lip
young: a small grey-green plant with oblong pebbled leaves in opposite pairs
crop: a low spreading grey-green bush, woody at the base
flower: upright spikes with spaced rings of violet-blue flowers held above the grey leaves

look_alikes: Meadow clary has green leaves in a ground rosette and bigger, strongly hooked flowers. Lamb's ears is far woollier and whiter with pink-purple flowers. Clary sage has huge leaves and pale pink-lilac flowers with large coloured bracts.
